Cybersecurity regulators have stated that tech giants need to do more to combat sextortion, specifically naming companies such as Apple, Meta, and Google, accusing them of not doing enough.

Victims of sextortion are often very young, including children under the age of 16...

A typical sextortion attack method involves the impersonator pretending to be of a similar age to the victim, flirting with them online. During this process, the attacker will send a nude photo claiming to be of themselves, and lure the victim into responding.

If the victim does send a photo back, the attacker will threaten to make it public, usually claiming they will send copies to the victim's family and friends via social media, unless the victim pays a ransom in exchange for deleting the photo.

According to TNW, Australia's cybersecurity regulator eSafety said that tech giants have not done enough in detecting this type of attack.

Taking Apple as an example, the regulator believes Apple should attempt to detect such scam messages sent via iMessage, just as it detects nude photos sent to children. The report also pointed out that Apple needs to make it easier for victims to report such attacks.

The regulator indicated that the problem is very severe, with over 10 percent of teenagers aged 16 to 18 having been victims, of whom more than half were harmed before the age of 16.

9to5Mac's perspective

The scale of this problem appears shocking, and there have been cases of teenagers taking their own lives due to sextortion. I agree with the regulator's view that tech giants, including Apple, should take more action to combat this type of crime.

iMessage messages use end-to-end encryption. However, Apple's existing technology for detecting nude photos shows that the company can perform on-device analysis on the recipient's device without compromising privacy. Similar methods could also be used to detect such scam messages.

Apple may have already begun addressing this issue. Developers have discovered a malicious message detection feature in iOS 26.6 beta 5.
